name: Carousel
description: A carousel ENGINE (useCarousel + Carousel* slot primitives) over a no-JS scroll-snap track, wearing the design's own slides, arrows and dots — plus a styled Carousel wrapper for designs that drew no gallery UI of their own.
whenToUse: Designs that show a ROW of slides one or a few at a time, scrolled sideways. Author the frame's OWN markup and drive it with useCarousel + the primitives: CarouselTrack is the scroll-snap mechanism (swipes with no JS), CarouselNext/CarouselPrev asChild make the design's drawn arrows the controls — mount BOTH even when the frame draws one, because a directional control renders exactly when it has a target, so the lone arrow's mirror appears once a slide is behind — and CarouselDot wears the design's own markers. autoAdvanceMs comes from the design's own timing, never invented, and refuses to run without a CarouselPause mounted. The styled Carousel component is the fallback for a design that drew no gallery UI — never the thing to reshape a designed section around. NOT for a row of cards that all fit at once (grid), cards stacked and driven by scroll (ScrollStack), or an ordered flow (StepFlow).

implements.note: START FROM skeleton.carousel-arrows.tsx beside this file: copy it into a section, reshape every element and class to the design, keep the hook and primitives. The track scrolls and snaps with no JavaScript; render only the controls the design draws (arrows without dots is common, dots without arrows too), and mount both arrows — the lone drawn arrow's mirror appears exactly when a slide is behind. Use the styled Carousel only when the design drew no gallery UI at all.

START FROM skeleton.carousel-auto.tsx beside this file, same contract. autoAdvanceMs comes from the design's own AFTER_TIMEOUT delay — never invent an interval; omitting it is correct when the design does not specify one. A CarouselPause must be mounted (the engine refuses the timer without one); auto-advance already pauses on hover/focus and stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
